title: automation trigger door silently drops a non-object `params` (string or array) and dispatches the flow with an empty params bag
body:
Filing gate: ① a product defect with a live reproduction. Silent input coercion, finding class (a).
Business reason: a caller that sends `params` in the wrong shape gets the flow run anyway with no inputs. Either it fails later with a misleading "Unknown variable" or, worse, it succeeds doing the wrong thing. The resume door already refuses the same value-shape class (#9416), so the two doors of one engine disagree.
Reader: the `packages/runtime` automation domain (`buildAutomationContext` drops the value); the next PR touching trigger input handling.
Dedupe (open AND closed): "trigger params non-object silently dropped flow dispatch" → 6 hits, none of them this one.
reach: public HTTP entry, measured on a fresh stock showcase boot, `main` 6679644a, as admin.
Checklist item priority: P1
type: Bug
QA-source: #25817 · automation.trigger-status-contract · observed beside the clauses

Reproduction:
1. As admin, send `POST /api/v1/automation/showcase_notify_owner/trigger` with `{"params":"oops"}`. The flow dispatches with an empty params bag and fails with `400 FLOW_FAILED`, "Unknown variable: ownerId".
2. `{"params":[1,2]}` behaves the same way.
3. Contrast: the resume door, given a non-object `inputs`, answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` before anything runs.

**Expected:** `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` that names `params` as not an object, before dispatch, and no run row.
